html:
The Kichwa Lamista are a Quechua-speaking people of the San Martín region of Peru, centred on the town of Lamas, where the Andes drop into the Amazon forest. Their language is a lowland variety of Quechua.

Their own tradition says their ancestors were Chanka people who fled into the forest to escape the expanding Inca Empire in the 1400s. Others think Quechua spread here later, through Spanish missions and trade. They farm in the forest, are known for their bright dress and music, and still live in a district of Lamas of their own.
